whatItDoes: Teutonic is a king-of-the-hill pretraining contest on Bittensor. Miners train language models and submit immutable checkpoints; a validator verifies each submission and sends challenger plus current king to a remote GPU evaluator for paired cross-entropy scoring. Whoever beats the king becomes king and earns the subnet's emissions; buyers get progressively better pretrained models.
hardwareRec: 8× H200/B200-class node (~141GB+ VRAM aggregate) to train a competitive checkpoint — per input metadata; training is done on your own infrastructure, since evaluation runs remotely on validator GPUs. Rental marketplaces not addressed by the README.
keyRequirements: Ed25519 hotkey (validator encrypts R2 upload credentials to it)
One submission per hotkey — consumed irreversibly at 'ready'
Complete checkpoint directory: no symlinks, no self-made manifest.json
Registration on netuid 3 can spend TAO (registration burn)
Choose competition lane: main, math, code, or text
minerJob: Day-to-day you train a model offline, then run the teutonic-miner CLI: register the Ed25519 hotkey, poll the mailbox for temporary prefix-scoped R2 credentials (7-day validity, auto-renewed), upload the checkpoint, then commit with 'ready'. 'Ready' is irreversible: the submission is consumed and the validator evaluates asynchronously. The evaluator scores challenger vs king with paired cross-entropy; a successful challenger becomes king and the validator updates weights. Rewards flow only if your checkpoint is or becomes the king.
minerJobProvide: Immutable trained model checkpoints uploaded to R2
One ready submission per hotkey per competition
Checkpoints that beat the king's cross-entropy
top10Strategy: Near winner-take-all: only the king earns, so marginal models waste your one submission. Newcomers win with training compute, data quality, and picking the lane (main/math/code/text) where they can beat the incumbent — not with CLI tricks. Understand the evaluation reuse limit and threshold mechanics before spending a registration; a rejected checkpoint can have its storage deleted automatically.
top10Levers: Tracking king state and thresholds before committing
followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/3 for the king UID and weight distribution, teutonic.ai for published state, and github.com/unarbos/teutonic commit cadence (thresholds, competitions, DEPLOY.md changes). One submission per hotkey makes timing king-targeted attempts everything.

whatItDoes: IOTA (Macrocosmos) pretrained LLMs across a swarm of heterogeneous machines: an orchestrator distributes model layers to miners and streams activations between them over a shared S3 bucket. Miners compete to process the most activations; validators spot-check that work was genuinely done. Currently training a 1.5B Llama-architecture model, with 15B-100B runs planned.
hardwareRec: CUDA GPU >=16GB VRAM (RTX 4090 cited by repo), Ubuntu 22.04. bf16 footprint ~2GB per 1B params today; larger planned runs will raise the bar. One GPU joins a pipeline stage; README silent on rental marketplaces.
keyRequirements: CUDA GPU >=16GB VRAM (RTX 4090 example)
Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy)
uv + bash setup.sh, then .env config
Sustained connectivity to orchestrator and shared S3
Run under PM2 for reliability
minerJob: You run start_miner.sh: the miner registers with the orchestrator, receives its assigned model layers, and streams activations for forward/backward passes. Miners race to process as many activations as possible each training stage, periodically upload local weights, and merge activations via a Butterfly All-Reduce variant. Validators spot-check miners to confirm assigned work was performed as required; emission flows per verified processing contribution across the multi-week run.
minerJobProvide: Processed activation batches per training step
Correct local weight updates uploaded on schedule
Uptime across long uninterrupted training runs
top10Strategy: Throughput-plus-reliability race: rewards track activations processed without failing spot-checks, so a pegged GPU, fast network path to orchestrator/S3, and zero downtime beat raw clock speed alone. Newcomers: follow the official IOTA mining setup guide exactly, monitor the public dashboard, and fix disconnects fast — every missed stream is lost paid work.
followTopMiners: Watch iota.macrocosmos.ai/dashboard/mainnet for miner counts and run metrics, taostats.io/subnet/9 for top UIDs and incentive spread, docs.macrocosmos.ai for setup-guide changes, and the repo commit cadence for run upgrades.

whatItDoes: ORO evaluates AI shopping agents on real-world shopping tasks (ORO Bench, from ShoppingBench). Miners submit Python agents that shop for a simulated shopper: search a frozen catalog, ask about unstated needs, track price/stock changes, and place one order. Validators run agents in sandboxed Docker; the best agent earns emissions. Challengers must clear a decaying threshold to take the top spot.
hardwareRec: CPU-only to host the agent — it can call LLM APIs (bring your own inference credentials; models must be on the live Backend allowlist). Validators need Docker + 16-32GB RAM. No GPU mentioned anywhere; a small VPS works.
keyRequirements: Python agent defining agent_main(problem_data)
Docker for local testing against the practice EnvPack
Inference credentials in .env (INFERENCE_PROVIDER)
Model must be on the live Backend allowlist
Beat the decaying challenger threshold to claim top spot
minerJob: You develop and host a Python agent that reads policy_view.tools and drives a shopping session — search, read listings, message the shopper, order — until done=true. Validators run it in isolated Docker sandboxes against sealed ORO Bench EnvPack tasks; a miss scores 0, a passing order earns up to 1.0 minus penalties for extra questions or a less-than-best pick. Emissions flow proportionally to validator stake-weighted scores; the reference implementation lives in src/agent/environment_agent.py.
minerJobProvide: Iterated submissions that clear the threshold
top10Strategy: An agent-quality knife fight, not an infra race: winning means asking exactly the right questions and picking the best product. Newcomers should fork the reference agent, replay failures via the local trajectories.html artifacts, fix each failure category, and iterate — the decaying threshold lets a steadily improving challenger dethrone a stale leader.
top10Levers: Local Docker testing on the practice EnvPack
LLM model choice within the allowlist
followTopMiners: Track the leaderboard at oroagents.com, docs.oroagents.com/docs/miners/scoring for threshold/scoring changes, repo commits (EnvPack versioning), and the ORO Discord (discord.gg/MHqAVWTdka).

whatItDoes: Desearch builds a pre-query web index for AI on Bittensor. In the live 2.0 phase miners crawl assigned pages and upload extracted text; validators re-check a sample under published rules; the Desearch team integrates accepted pages into the index behind its Search API (console.desearch.ai). Miners are paid by their share of accepted pages. Embedding tasks are built and open later.
hardwareRec: CPU-only for the crawl phase: any cheap VPS with bandwidth and disk. The later embed program will pay miners to run the selected embedding model on GPUs, so keep a modest GPU option in mind. Rentals fine.
keyRequirements: Registered hotkey on SN22 + task API access (docs/miner-setup.md)
Fetch assigned pages and upload extracted text
Validators re-fetch random samples; mismatch forfeits earnings since last good check
All results public at api-22.desearch.ai/v1/tasks
Local miner test before registering (test-your-miner.md)
minerJob: The miner takes tasks from the task API, fetches its assigned URLs, extracts clean text, and uploads it for the index. Validators re-fetch a random sample of each miner's tasks and compare; weights are set from the share of accepted work, and a miner caught returning bad pages loses everything earned since its last good check. A future embed task type will run a selected model on accepted text with sample recomputation. Reward = your share of accepted pages per round.
minerJobProvide: Fetched page text for assigned URLs
Later: embeddings from the selected model
top10Strategy: A crawl-reliability war: fetch success rate on hard pages, extraction accuracy, and throughput decide your accepted share. Newcomers: run the reference miner, pass the local validator test first, then tune concurrency and IP quality. Never shortcut pages — sampling makes cheating lose everything since the last good check.
top10Levers: Fetch success rate on assigned pages
Fast adoption of new task types (embed)
followTopMiners: Watch the public task log api-22.desearch.ai/v1/tasks, docs/emission.md for share mechanics, taostats.io/subnet/22 for incentive distribution, and the Desearch Discord/X for program openings (embedding phase).

whatItDoes: gm is an LLM API gateway: buyers point existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini SDKs at the gm gateway and get identical behavior. Miners supply upstream provider API capacity inside an Intel TDX TEE (neither operators nor hosts see buyer content or miner keys) and earn the spread between buyer price and upstream cost.
hardwareRec: No GPU, no bare metal: the miner is a pinned TEE container deployed to Phala Cloud (bring a funded Phala account). Hardware here means upstream API keys plus TDX attestation. Rentals irrelevant; Phala is the supported target.
keyRequirements: Funded Phala Cloud account; deploy via gmcli (dstack compose)
Your own provider API keys: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Chutes, Z.ai, Moonshot, DeepInfra, KubeTEE, Engy, Moonmath, NEAR
Taostats OAuth login (device code)
Registered Bittensor hotkey recorded with gmcli
Intel TDX TEE attestation must stay green
minerJob: You deploy the gm-miner image to Phala Cloud with gmcli deploy; at startup it mints an RA-TLS data-plane certificate, runs the attestation server, optional NEAR/Chutes/KubeTEE verifiers, and the Envoy data plane inside TDX. Buyer requests route to your verified key slots (up to 8 keys per direct route); you declare products and prices via gmcli and earn the spread on served traffic. Keys stay encrypted inside the TEE; testnet is netuid 482.
minerJobProvide: Upstream LLM API capacity inside the TEE container
Valid TDX attestation for the data plane
Reliable multi-key slot capacity per route
top10Strategy: This is a margins-and-reliability business, not a benchmark race: price spreads per model, multi-provider route coverage, and uptime decide earnings. Newcomers: rehearse fully on testnet first, source cheap upstreams (DeepInfra/Engy/Moonmath sourcing routes) for popular models, and use multi-key slots to survive rate limits.
top10Levers: Price spread vs upstream cost per model
followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/28 for earning hotkeys, saygm.com and the repo docs/ for product/route changes, and release cadence of gm-miner (run gmcli update; the image is pinned to digest).

whatItDoes: Aurelius is a moral-reasoning alignment subnet. Miners submit structured ethical-dilemma scenario configs; validators score them through an 8-stage pipeline (schema, rate-limit, novelty, classifier, simulation) and run accepted scenarios through DeepMind Concordia generative-agent simulations. Transcripts become training data that improves LLM performance on moral-reasoning benchmarks (MoReBench).
hardwareRec: CPU-only for miners: a Docker host with a public IP (axon port 8091). The validator side uses an OpenAI-compatible LLM API (DeepSeek default, cheapest) instead of local GPUs. No GPU requirement found for miners; a small VPS is enough.
keyRequirements: Hotkey registered on netuid 37 (registration costs TAO)
Docker 20.10+; published GHCR miner image
Scenario config library loaded at startup (schema_v1: 9 tension archetypes, 2 agents, 1-10 scenes)
Work-token balance that validators can spend on acceptance
Publicly reachable IP + open inbound port 8091
minerJob: You run the aurelius-miner container serving operator-authored scenario JSONs from a configs/ directory in round-robin order, each stamped with a work_id and hotkey-signed via ScenarioConfigSynapse. The validator charges work tokens, pushes each config through the 8-stage pipeline including a Concordia simulation sidecar, and sets weights on outcomes. Miners never generate configs at request time — quality authoring happens offline and the container restarts to pick up additions.
minerJobProvide: Novel scenarios that pass novelty/classifier gates
top10Strategy: A content-quality war: duplicate or template-y scenarios die at novelty/classifier stages, so breadth across the 9 archetypes plus genuinely fresh premises wins. Newcomers: study testlab configs in the aurelius-ops repo, author programmatically (seed_generator.py as reference), keep a large diverse library, and budget work tokens.
top10Levers: Scenario novelty vs validator dedup gates
followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/37 weights, the repo's commit cadence for pipeline-stage and threshold changes, GHCR image tags (aurelius-miner:latest), and aurelius-ops testlab configs for what currently passes.

whatItDoes: AlphaRidge reads the world's financial news — about 290,000 articles a day from ~13,000 sources — and turns it into structured market data powering the AlphaRidge product (charts, screener, events browser, API). Miners produce per-article analysis: asset sentiment, Wikidata/ticker entity resolution, economic data points, contagion chains, narrative tags, embeddings.
hardwareRec: 8GB VRAM minimum, 24GB+ comfortable (RTX 4090 fits); 16-32GB RAM, 8-16+ CPU cores, 60-100GB disk. ~44GB of models download on first run. NER stage is CPU-heavy: core count sets throughput, and throughput is what you're paid for. Rentals acceptable.
keyRequirements: OpenRouter API key — you pay your own LLM inference (2 of 4 pipeline stages)
Registered hotkey on netuid 45
Return batch leases in time; late batches requeue to others
Batch audits: whole batch discarded if the validator's blind sample doesn't reproduce
Reputation multiplier gates pay; penalties can zero a window
minerJob: Run neurons.miner with the analyzer pipeline (spaCy transformer NER, ReFinED entity linking, two LLM stages via OpenRouter). Validators lease batches; you analyze at roughly 12-18s per article. The validator blind-re-runs a sample of each batch and discards the entire batch on mismatch. Pay = verified volume × reputation (EMA through a logistic gate), priced in USD per point rather than alpha. Batch size ramps with demonstrated throughput; multiple UIDs do not multiply pay.
top10Strategy: Throughput × quality economics: more CPU cores and faster, cheaper LLM calls raise verified volume; a single failed audit wastes the batch and dents reputation. Newcomers: expect tiny first batches that ramp, budget OpenRouter spend carefully, fix NAT/nginx header quirks, and watch the observatory leaderboard to see reputation as validators do.
top10Levers: Batch audit pass rate protecting reputation
followTopMiners: Track the miner leaderboard on alpharidge.ai (live throughput + reputation), taostats.io/subnet/45 for incentive spread, and repo commits for pipeline/model changes.

whatItDoes: Lium is a decentralized GPU rental marketplace on Bittensor: providers list NVIDIA GPUs that renters (people, teams, AI agents) book hourly at lium.io. A validator checks every node every 15 minutes (hardware, GPU, network, ports, Sysbox runtime). Providers earn rental-fee share plus subnet emission, including idle pay for eligible unrented GPUs.
hardwareRec: Any NVIDIA model on the validator's supported GPU_MODEL_RATES list (input suggests 8× B300 for top tiers; consumer RTX 30/40/50-series listed). Ubuntu 24.04, Sysbox, Docker, public IP, >=100Mbps; idle pay needs disk >=1.5× VRAM. TDX only for H100/H200/B200/GB200 tiers.
keyRequirements: Registered hotkey on SN51 (dynamic fee) + Provider Portal sign-in
Central Provider Server selected AND Discord connected — otherwise zero incentive
Sysbox runtime + NVIDIA Container Toolkit (validator rejects otherwise)
Ports: node HTTP, SSH 2200, and >=3 renting ports reachable from internet
Idle pool: price at/below market soft limit, disk >=1.5× VRAM, power-limit support
minerJob: Run `lium mine` on each GPU host: it installs the CLI, writes neurons/executor/.env, starts the node agent under docker compose, and self-checks. The single team-run validator SSHes in every 15 minutes to verify hardware/GPU/network/ports, create and remove rental pods, and report results. Emission splits three ways: rented pool (scored by GPU model/count), unrented pool (eligible idle GPUs), and burn. Rental income pays daily to your coldkey; emission pays per tempo to the hotkey.
minerJobProvide: Validator-passing GPU nodes under Sysbox isolation
Reachable renting ports for tenant pods
top10Strategy: Marketplace capacity play: chain data shows the top-10 providers capture ~99% of incentive, so scale matters — many validator-clean nodes, good bandwidth, and market-priced listings. Newcomers: start with one consumer card to learn validator reason codes (INSUFFICIENT_PORTS, VERIFYX speed, sysbox failures), then scale only what passes consistently.
top10Levers: Pricing vs market soft limit for idle pool
followTopMiners: Track provider.lium.io/rewards-calculator (live rates), the public node feed lium.io/api/public/v1/nodes, docs.lium.io/providers/rewards, taostats.io/subnet/51 top UIDs, and the Lium Discord #tickets for policy changes.

whatItDoes: Attune (Robotensor) is a robot-foundation-model subnet. First competition 'Vector': a policy (vector_v1.1) sees one demonstration of a task and must repeat it in a different scene. Miners submit policy weights on Hugging Face; validators duel each challenger against the current king in RoboTwin simulation; the lane's rewards go to the four most recent champions (40/30/20/10).
hardwareRec: Submission is only an HF repo + on-chain commit, but training a competitive vector_v1.1 policy needs real GPU (validator duel units use up to 34GB each; 1 unit/GPU). Rented GPU pods explicitly supported (vast.ai, lium.io via docker/build.sh) — rentals allowed.
keyRequirements: HF repo containing only model.safetensors (pinned tensors, no quantization tricks)
On-chain commitment with revision + sha256 digest (attune miner commit)
One submission per hotkey; earliest identical-weights commitment wins
Repo must stay public and unchanged — deletion dethrones and burns the share
Challenger must beat king by 3+ points avg success over 160 seeded units
minerJob: Train a vector_v1.1 policy, validate locally with attune miner check, upload to a public HF repo, then commit the `vector:<owner>/<repo>@<commit>.<digest>` string on-chain (commit before making public — earliest wins). The validator queues commitments oldest-first and duels each against the king on 160 units seeded from a finalized block. Rewards: lane share split 40/30/20/10 across the 4 most recent champions; weights are safetensors-only, never executed.
minerJobProvide: vector_v1.1 model.safetensors on a public HF repo
On-chain sha256 commitment matching the weights
Policies beating the king by 3+ points
Repo kept public/unchanged while holding a place
top10Strategy: Research race with a forgiving payout curve: four champion slots mean reaching top-4 once pays, and champion places decay only as newer champions arrive. Newcomers: start from the pinned vector_v1.1 spec, train on RoboTwin-Vector tasks, run pod-check --selftest on rented pods, and target the +3-point margin rather than perfection.
top10Levers: Policy training compute (rented GPU pods OK)
Commit hygiene (digest, public repo, earliest wins)
followTopMiners: Track the champion list via attune miner status / on-chain weights, the vector-orchestrator and RoboTwin-Vector repos for spec bumps, and current champions' HF repos for architecture hints.

whatItDoes: TPN (True Performance Network) incentivizes miners to build high-performance quantized language models. It runs recurring competitions with defined benchmarks, scoring windows and emission distributions. Miners benchmark their own GGUF models and submit the model plus benchmark run ids via a TimeLocked Commit — hidden until scoring so submissions can't be copied — and validators verify and rank verified scores.
hardwareRec: GPU for building/quantizing/testing GGUF models locally (size depends on competition); note the graded benchmarks run on the subnet's paid benchmark service, not your box, so no huge inference rig is strictly required. HF account required. Rentals fine for training/quantization.
keyRequirements: tpn CLI + hotkey registered on netuid 65
One .gguf per private HF repo (upload metadata saved)
BENCHMARK_API_KEY with credits — you pay for your own benchmark runs
TimeLocked Commit with run ids; auto-reveals at commit_end_block
Publish the HF repo public before the scoring phase; optional miner collateral
minerJob: Workflow via tpn: register, upload your .gguf to a private HF repo, run `tpn benchmark` (quotes each required benchmark against your credit, saves run ids), `tpn commit` the TimeLocked payload on chain, then `tpn publish` before scoring. Validators verify every run id benchmarked exactly the committed repo/revision/file, then check top candidates for RAM usage, file integrity and base-model provenance before distributing emissions by verified rank. Incomplete runs at scoring time score 0.
minerJobProvide: Quantized GGUF models matched to each competition
Paid benchmark run ids matching the commit exactly
Public HF repo before the scoring phase
top10Strategy: Quantization craft plus benchmark economics: maximize benchmark score per RAM-usage constraint, and cheaply re-run single weak benchmarks (--only X --rerun) to replace bad runs. Newcomers: read docs/Overview.md, start from strong provenance-clean base models, budget credits before committing, and never miss the scoring-phase deadline.
followTopMiners: Watch `tpn competitions --all` and the leader validator API (val0.trueperformancenetwork.com) for active competitions and leaderboards, docs/Miner.md changes, and taostats.io/subnet/65 for emission distribution.

whatItDoes: NATIX StreetVision is a decentralized image-classification subnet: miners run binary classifiers that detect roadwork/construction sites in images, outputting a float 0-1 (above 0.5 = roadwork). Validators challenge miners with balanced mixes of real and synthetic media and reward accuracy. The subnet powers construction-site detection for NATIX applications.
hardwareRec: Entry-level GPU suffices: input metadata cites GTX 1660 Super 4GB; any small CUDA card runs the classifiers. Model submissions go to HuggingFace; resubmit within 90 days to keep reward factor 1. Consumer setups and rentals both fine.
keyRequirements: Registered hotkey; axon answering image queries with [0,1] floats
Public HuggingFace model submission required
90-day validity: reward factor 1, then decays to zero
Robustness to synthetic/generated images in validator challenge pools
Continuous retraining/re-submission culture
minerJob: Serve an axon that scores incoming images for roadwork presence. Validators send balanced real+synthetic batches (new datasets and generative models are continually added on the validator side, config in natix/validator/config.py) and grade accuracy; weights follow accuracy multiplied by your model's time-decay reward factor. Day-to-day: keep the axon online, retrain improved classifiers, and re-submit to HuggingFace before the 90-day decay bites.
top10Strategy: Accuracy race against an evolving synthetic challenge set: fine-tune on diverse real and generated data, calibrate the 0.5 threshold, and maintain a retraining cadence so the 90-day decay never erodes your factor. Newcomers can start on a 4GB card; the NATIX HuggingFace org and W&B logs provide baselines.
followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/72 weights, wandb.ai/natix_network for validation metrics, the natix-network-org HuggingFace for baselines, and the NATIX Discord for dataset/model updates.

whatItDoes: MVTRX/τaos runs an agent-based market simulation: miners host trading strategies inside a C++ limit-order-book simulator with L3 data and background agents, scored on intraday Kappa-3 (risk-adjusted) with minimum trading volume. Optional GenTRX adds distributed training of a shared order-book generative model (~5% pool). An alpha-token exchange is a later release.
hardwareRec: CPU-only for trading: no set requirements; base tooling ~1GB RAM per miner instance (VPS works). Optional NVIDIA 6-8GB VRAM GPU for GenTRX training; CPU-only training supported but may miss deadlines. No GPU for the main 95% pool.
keyRequirements: Custom agent class loaded from ~/.taos/agents (subclass GenTRXAgent for training opt-in)
Respond to every state-update tick; response latency sets execution slippage
Maintain minimum cumulative round-trip volume for full scoring
Rolling-window scores persist across weekly simulation configurations
GenTRX: S3 bucket for compressed gradient uploads
minerJob: Your agent receives L3 order-book state updates from validators each tick and returns place/cancel instructions; the simulation pauses while awaiting you, and your response time determines the delay (slippage) applied to your orders. Scores use intraday Kappa-3 plus activity requirements, on a rolling window across runs that reset weekly. GenTRX opt-in trains the shared model on your assigned data slice in a background thread and uploads compressed gradients to a personal S3 bucket for validator scoring (~95/5 pool split).
minerJobProvide: Trading-agent order instructions per state tick
Risk-managed positive Kappa-3 across market realizations
top10Strategy: A pure quant-skill war: market-making with tight risk control, fast responses to minimize slippage, and strategies robust to weekly re-parameterized markets. Newcomers: start from example agents, backtest offline against the local proxy background model, then layer GenTRX for the extra training pool with zero trade-off against trading rewards.
followTopMiners: Watch the Grafana dashboards (taos.simulate.trading, mvtrx.simulate.trading), taostats.io/subnet/79 for weights, the repo's agents/ directory and config releases, and the taos Discord for parameter-change announcements.

whatItDoes: InfiniteQuant is a signal market: miners commit encrypted directional trade calls (2-hour drand timelock), validators grade them against real market candles, and emissions go to miners with statistically proven edge — Wilson lower-bound hit-rate >=50% on enough decisive trades, scaled by hit-rate tiers. Two mechanisms: low-frequency (3 calls/day) and high-frequency (30 calls/day).
hardwareRec: CPU only: Python 3.10 venv on any small VPS. No GPU, no market-data subscription (validators handle all pricing). Feed token comes via Telegram bot; the miner is non-custodial and extremely lightweight. Rentals irrelevant.
keyRequirements: 3 signals/day per hotkey, 1h minimum gap (LF); TP/SL symmetric 1:1 per-asset bands
Unrevealed blob = decisive LOSS; 3 bad blobs in 30d zeroes the hotkey 30 days
8-day warmup: dust weight, warmup wins never pay
Copy penalty: shadowing an existing (pair, direction) voids copied wins
HF mode: 50 submissions over 8 distinct days + per-pair direction diversity gates
minerJob: Pick a pair and direction, encrypt the signal with the 2-hour drand timelock, and put SHA256(signal) on-chain via set_commitment (entry price derives from the commit block). After reveal, validators verify the plaintext against the hash and grade on 1-minute candles: TP first = WON, SL first = LOST, neither = WASH. Weight ∝ trailing-7-day qualified wins (cap 20, linear decay) × shrunk-hit-rate tier (1.0×/1.2×/2.0×). HF mode sends signed WebSocket frames with countersigned receipts and Merkle-rooted windows.
top10Strategy: Real forecasting edge, not infrastructure: with 3 calls/day, selectivity and conviction matter — tiers reward 60% (1.2×) and 70% (2.0×) shrunk hit-rates, and luck cannot qualify. Newcomers: use the 8-day warmup to build a record free, respect the copy penalty by being first, and add the HF board only with genuine two-sided discipline.
followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/89 weights and top UIDs, the repo's release cadence and config.SUBMISSION_RULES_HISTORY / signals-bands.json updates, and the Telegram bot (@Iqsignals2026_bot) community for rule changes.

whatItDoes: Distil (SN97, formerly branded Albedo) is a king-of-the-hill competitive model-distillation subnet. The teacher is moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 (1T total / ~32B active MoE; Qwen3.5/3.6 teacher cutover went live 2026-05-02). Miners distill <=33B students, upload to HuggingFace and commit on-chain; validators score a 25+ axis composite; winner takes 100% of emissions.
hardwareRec: Student-side bf16 training of 33B-class students: 4-8× H100/H200; LoRA + checkpointing fits smaller rigs. 2× 24GB only for sub-2B sanity runs. Quantized students (GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF) rejected. Training infra is your choice; rentals allowed, evaluation runs on validator GPUs.
keyRequirements: Kimi-family architecture + Kimi BPE tokenizer (vocab 163,840), <=33B total params, safetensors bf16/fp16
One PERMANENT commitment per hotkey (new attempts need a new hotkey)
Unique weights: SHA256 + activation-fingerprint near-copy detection
Model stays public and unchanged on HF — edits = DQ
Ranking key: composite.final = 0.75 × worst-3-axis mean + 0.25 × weighted mean
minerJob: Train a distilled student, run test_miner.py (the same 15 validator checks locally), then commit the HF repo link on-chain (miner.py, dry-run first). Each commitment is scored exactly once: 11 procedurally-generated block-seeded axes (~50% — math, code, reasoning, long-context, knowledge, honesty), distillation tier (~30% incl. on-policy RKL), judge/quality and discipline axes. The king is re-evaluated every round on the same items; a challenger dethrones only at a 5% margin. Weight 1.0 to the king, 0 to everyone else.
minerJobProvide: Distilled <=33B Kimi-family student on a public HF repo
All 15 pre-submission checks passed before committing
top10Strategy: Winner-take-all research problem: because 75% of the score is your three WORST axes, balanced students beat specialists — fix your weakest capability, don't polish KL. Newcomers: use on-policy RKL training (community script in examples/), pre-check everything locally to save registration burns, and budget for multiple hotkey attempts since commitments can't change.
top10Levers: Balanced quality across all axes (worst-3 rule)
Robustness to procedural block-seeded axes (no overfitting)
followTopMiners: Watch distil.arbos.life (composite scores, king) and api.arbos.life, chat.arbos.life to query the current king, docs/MINER_FAQ.md and reports/ in the repo for axis changes, and taostats.io/subnet/97 for weight flips.

whatItDoes: Beam (SN105) is a decentralized bandwidth coordination network: it moves data at scale between clouds (AWS S3, R2, GCS, Snowflake, APIs, webhooks, MCP). Orchestrators split transfers into chunks routed across worker nodes (fan-out, aggregation, mesh); every transfer generates Proof-of-Bandwidth that validators verify and convert into emission weights. Site reports ~760 Gb/s aggregate, 1.8PB moved, ~1,150 miners.
hardwareRec: CPU only: bandwidth is the resource, not GPU. A VPS or home server with strong sustained uplink/downlink, stable uptime and open ports is what earns. No GPU requirement found; rentals irrelevant since network throughput, not compute, is scored.

Rewards scale with measured, verified bandwidth contribution — the public reference covers transfer assignment, PRISM scoring and weight materialization.
